copy.twitter: Stop organizing your lit review by author. It’s a book report, not a dissertation. Group by themes and debates to actually show critical thinking. If you’re stuck, how are you currently managing your reading notes? Let’s fix your workflow.
copy.facebook:
If your literature review feels like a list of 'Author X said this, then Author Y said that,' you’re falling into the 54% trap. It’s the most common mistake I see, and it’s an easy fix once you shift your perspective.

THE 54% TRAP: Writing chapter sections organized by individual authors or years, providing descriptive book reports with zero critical comparison of methodologies.

THE 1ST CLASS BLUEPRINT: Thematic coding: Organizing chapters by theoretical debates, comparing sampling limitations across studies, and clearly highlighting the empirical knowledge gap.

When you stop summarizing and start synthesizing, you aren't just showing you read the material—you’re showing you can lead the conversation. That’s where the high marks live.
